articles.title: Travis Kelce’s $5.35 million mansion faces new developments as officials schedule another property review
articles.summary: Travis Kelce’s $5.35 million Ohio mansion offers the privacy and luxury expected of an NFL star, but making the estate more secluded has proved
articles.body: Travis Kelce’s $5.35 million Ohio mansion offers the privacy and luxury expected of an NFL star, but making the estate more secluded has proved complicated. The Kansas City Chiefs tight end now faces questions from local residents about landscaping, aging sewer lines and the impact of new barriers on the neighborhood. What began as an effort to improve the property has turned into a wider discussion about balancing personal space with community concerns. With another review scheduled for November, Kelce’s plans for his historic lakeside home remain partly unresolved, despite progress on one major renovation proposal.Travis Kelce’s Ohio mansion draws attention over privacy plansKelce purchased the 3.5-acre Bratenahl estate on March 2, 2026, for $5.35 million. Located along Lake Erie near Cleveland, the property stands out for its scale, history and impressive facilities.Known as Moyenage, the mansion dates back to 1904. The historic residence spans 21,140 square feet and features eight bedrooms, 11 bathrooms, seven fireplaces, a sauna, a fitness centre and a heated outdoor pool. Its grounds also include a five-car garage and a guest cottage created from a former gatehouse.However, improving security around such a large property comes with challenges. Kelce’s proposed fencing initially included an eight-foot barrier, prompting concerns from nearby homeowners about lake views and the appearance of the neighborhood.The revised design received unanimous approval from Bratenahl’s Architectural Review Board on September 8. The plan calls for a six-foot black aluminium fence covering approximately 1,190 linear feet, with matching gates and a design intended to complement existing stone walls.Contractor Jacob Kutz explained that the changes addressed residents’ objections, including concerns about preserving views of Lake Erie. The fence will also sit about two feet inside the property boundary to avoid interfering with shared sewer infrastructure.Travis Kelce’s landscaping proposal faces fresh questionsAlthough the fence has received approval, the mansion’s landscaping plans have encountered further delays. During an October 6 meeting, village officials examined a proposal to plant evergreen trees behind the property.Residents raised concerns about the trees’ eventual height and their possible impact on neighboring homes. Officials indicated that plants growing below 10 feet could offer privacy without creating the same problems. The board approved the front-yard landscaping but postponed its decision on the rear section.Shared utilities have also become a point of contention. Neighbor Katherine Bolton warned that roots from roughly 50 proposed evergreens could damage an aging sewer line reportedly shared with the estate. She said protecting her section of the pipe could cost $75,000.Kelce’s representatives have discussed a $7,500 repair to part of the shared sewer, and the fence design includes access gates for maintenance crews.Bratenahl’s Architectural Review Board plans to reconsider the landscaping proposal on November 10, 2026. Until then, Kelce’s efforts to improve privacy at Moyenage remain subject to local review and the concerns of those living nearby.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: “WHAT she’s done for women’s sports....": Patrick Mahomes shows his support for Brittany Mahomes’ growing career beyond the NFL
articles.summary: Patrick Mahomes knows how to make a statement without saying much.
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes knows how to make a statement without saying much. The Kansas City Chiefs quarterback recently showed his support for wife Brittany Mahomes after she shared fresh photos from an Adidas shoot on Instagram. His response was brief, but the message was clear. The three-time Super Bowl champion left two heart-eyes emojis beneath her post, drawing attention to Brittany’s latest fashion and fitness appearance. Beyond their public moments as a couple, the two have also built a growing presence in professional sports, particularly through their involvement with women’s soccer in Kansas City.Patrick Mahomes reacts to Brittany Mahomes’ Adidas shootBrittany, 31, shared the Instagram carousel on Thursday, October 15, featuring several looks from her Adidas partnership. The photos highlighted her athletic style, with workout clothing, classic sportswear and gym-ready outfits taking centre stage.One picture showed her wearing a black unitard with Adidas’ signature white stripes. Another featured the former soccer player lifting weights in a black sports bra and leggings. Additional looks included navy blue and burgundy workout pieces.Brittany captioned the post, “Archives never expire ☺️,” giving the collection a playful touch.Patrick, also 31, quickly joined the conversation with the comment, “😍😍.” His response attracted attention from fans who follow the couple’s lives beyond the football field.Several familiar faces also praised Brittany’s post. Sports broadcaster Erin Andrews commented, “Meeeow,” while Charissa Thompson wrote, “There she isssss.”Patrick’s younger brother, Jackson Mahomes, focused on Brittany’s fitness progress, writing, “She been in the gym!!🔥🔥.” Tavia Hunt, wife of Chiefs chairman and CEO Clark Hunt, also showed her support with three heart emojis.This was not Patrick’s first public reaction to Brittany’s Adidas work. In August, he responded with “😍😍😍” after she shared another set of pictures connected to the brand’s collaboration with Dick’s Sporting Goods.Brittany Mahomes earns praise for her role in women’s sportsBrittany’s career extends well beyond modelling and fitness content. She is a founding co-owner of the Kansas City Current, a National Women’s Soccer League club she helped establish in 2020 alongside sports executives Angie and Chris Long.Patrick joined the club’s ownership group in 2023, adding another professional sports venture to the couple’s portfolio.Brittany also recently received public recognition from Kylie Kelce for her work supporting women’s sports in Kansas City. During an appearance on Michelle Obama and Craig Robinson’s “IMO” podcast, Kylie highlighted her contribution to the local soccer community.“Brittany Mahomes is a great example,” Kelce said. “WHAT she’s done for women’s sports and women’s soccer in the Kansas City area is so impressive.”Brittany responded through an Instagram story, writing, “Thank you!!! 🙏🏻🤍@kykelce.”While Patrick’s latest comment focused on his wife’s Adidas photos, their shared involvement in the Kansas City Current reflects a wider commitment to sports beyond the NFL. Together, they continue to support projects that connect their public profiles with their interests off the field.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Is Troy Aikman done with the Miami Dolphins? His uncertain ESPN future could bring him closer to a Dallas Cowboys return
articles.summary: Troy Aikman’s time advising the Miami Dolphins may already be over.
articles.body: Troy Aikman’s time advising the Miami Dolphins may already be over. The Pro Football Hall of Famer helped the franchise find its new general manager and head coach during the 2026 offseason. However, a report now suggests his consulting role came with a clear limit. With his future at ESPN also uncertain, could Aikman eventually find another way into an NFL front office?Currently, a return to the Dallas Cowboys remains a possibility. Still, the former Cowboys quarterback has previously expressed interest in working with an NFL team beyond his broadcasting career. His next move could depend on what happens after the 2026 season.Why Troy Aikman’s Miami Dolphins consulting role has endedAs per the Front Office Sports reporter Mark Maske, Troy Aikman’s official consulting arrangement with the Miami Dolphins covered the searches that led to the hiring of general manager Jon-Eric Sullivan and head coach Jeff Hafley during the 2026 offseason.Maske reported that it remains unclear whether Aikman continues to advise Dolphins owner Stephen Ross through his relationships with Ross, Hafley and Sullivan. Any continued involvement, however, would not fall under a formal consulting agreement, according to a source cited by Front Office Sports.Ross brought Aikman in to help with the team’s search. Aikman explained that Ross’ brother-in-law, Sillman, contacted several people to ask who could help the Dolphins. His name kept coming up, and he agreed to assist.The assignment also gave Troy Aikman a taste of NFL front-office work, something he had considered over the years. But he never announced plans to leave broadcasting for a full-time position in Miami.Could the Dallas Cowboys give Troy Aikman another chance?Aikman has made it clear that a full-time NFL role could interest him after broadcasting. However, the financial side could complicate that move.Front Office Sports reported that sources from multiple NFL teams consider it highly unlikely that a franchise would match the salary Troy Aikman earns in broadcasting. Reports put his ESPN salary at around $18 million annually, making a comparable front-office deal a difficult proposition.Meanwhile, Troy Aikman’s future in the broadcast booth remains uncertain. On October 17, 2026, he was still expected to work through the season before becoming a free agent at the end of the year. He previously said he would see what opportunities emerged after the season.That uncertainty has revived speculation about a possible Dallas Cowboys connection. Former Cowboys teammate Michael Irvin previously said Aikman wanted a John Elway-style role with Dallas. However, neither the Cowboys nor Aikman has confirmed any plan for a reunion.As of now, Troy Aikman’s consulting work in Miami appears to have reached its official end. Whether his next chapter involves ESPN, Dallas or another NFL opportunity remains an open question.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: “Since I was seven years old, I only wanted”: How Tom Brady’s childhood love for Don Mattingly cards inspired his growing trading card business beyond the NFL
articles.summary: Tom Brady has seven Super Bowl rings, but his love for baseball cards started long before his NFL career took off.
articles.body: Tom Brady has seven Super Bowl rings, but his love for baseball cards started long before his NFL career took off. As a child, he spent his money collecting cards of Don Mattingly, his favourite player. After years, Brady still owns that collection and sometimes brings it to CardVault store openings. What began as a childhood hobby has now become a business venture that keeps him connected to the sports collectibles world.Brady started collecting cards when he was around seven or eight years old. Growing up in San Mateo, California, he often visited a local hobby shop to add to his collection. The interest stayed with him through his football career and into retirement. At Fanatics Fest in New York in July 2026, he even got the chance to meet Mattingly and share the story behind his childhood collection.Tom Brady still holds on to his Don Mattingly collectionBrady did not hide his excitement when he met Mattingly at Fanatics Fest. The former New York Yankees star had been his favourite player since childhood, and his cards once filled the pages of Brady’s binder.“Since I was seven years old, I only wanted Don Mattingly cards,” Brady told Mattingly at Fanatics Fest in July 2026. He recalled how the cards filled the laminated pages of his childhood collection.Brady still holds on to that binder and sometimes brings it to CardVault store openings. Collecting also helped him develop a practical skill. During an interview with Front Office Sports at Fanatics Fest in July 2026, he joked that collecting baseball cards helped him become better at maths.For Brady, the appeal goes beyond owning valuable cards. He enjoys finding something new, following the players he admires and building a collection over time. Those childhood memories now connect directly to his work in the trading card industry. How Tom Brady turned his childhood hobby into CardVaultBrady joined CardVault as a co-owner in 2024. However, he wanted more than a single shop carrying his name. He saw an opportunity to expand the business and bring the collecting experience to more fans.During discussions about the partnership, Brady told CardVault cofounder Chris Costa, “I don’t want to do a store. I want to open all of them with you guys.” Costa recalled the exchange in an interview with Front Office SportsThe company planned to open its 17th store in Palo Alto, California, in August 2026. It also set a target of 40 locations by 2028, according to the report.Brady’s involvement goes beyond promoting the brand. Costa told that the two speak daily. Brady even worked the phones to improve CardVault’s allocation of Pokémon cards, which have become popular with customers.At Fanatics Fest in July 2026, Brady also spoke about customers saving money to buy cards, just as he did as a child. He wants them to enjoy the experience of finding something special.His NFL career made him a household name, but baseball cards have remained a personal passion. Through CardVault, Brady is turning that childhood interest into a business while helping a new generation of collectors discover the same excitement.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Will Saquon Barkley play against the Carolina Panthers today? Latest injury update on the Philadelphia Eagles' popular star
articles.summary: The Philadelphia Eagles have recorded a slow run on the field in the new season as the team battles through an injury plagued roster.
articles.body: The Philadelphia Eagles have recorded a slow run on the field in the new season as the team battles through an injury plagued roster. Though the Philadelphia Eagles started the new season strong with two consecutive victories, narrowly defeating the Washington Commanders (24–22) and the Tennessee Titans (24–20), they have since suffered three straight defeats. The team has now recorded consecutive losses against the Chicago Bears (7–27), the Los Angeles Rams (20–24), and the Jacksonville Jaguars (17–19). Ahead of the clash against the Carolina Panthers, all eyes remain on Saquon Barkley.Is Saquon Barkley fit enough to take the field for the Philadelphia Eagles as the team prepares to go against the Carolina Panthers?No, the Philadelphia Eagles’ star player Saquon Barkley will not play today. The team have officially ruled him out for today's Week 6 game against the Carolina Panthers due to a right hamstring injury.Apart from Saquon Barkley, starting quarterback Jalen Hurts was placed on injured reserve due to a blood clot in his calf.Joining him on the sidelines are star running back Saquon Barkley (hamstring), defensive back Michael Carter II (abdomen), and edge rusher Jalyx Hunt (knee/ankle), who have all been ruled out.The Philadelphia Eagles have also announced that guard Landon Dickerson (knee), cornerback Jakorian Bennett (knee), and tight ends Grant Calcaterra (back) and Eli Stowers (quad) will also sit out today after not being activated from injured reserve. On the defensive front, outside linebacker A.J. Epenesa (back) is officially out while center Drew Kendall (knee) remains the team's only active questionable player on the report.Saquon Barkley’s injury history and what really happened to him on the fieldThe Philadelphia Eagles’ star player Saquon Barkley suffered the injury during the Week 4 game against the Los Angeles Rams which forced him to miss the subsequent London game against the Jacksonville Jaguars.Saquon Barkley did not practice at all this week. He missed every single team practice session leading up to today's game due to his hamstring injury.The Philadelphia Eagles officially ruled him out on Friday marking this being his second consecutive game that he would be missing out on.A few days ago, the Philadelphia Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni reflected on Saquon Barkley’s situation as he said the star player will "do everything he can do to get himself back."Philadelphia Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni added, "Obviously, he's a great player and a great teammate," Sirianni said. "We always need him on the field."As per reports, the team expects Saquon Barkley will be healthy enough to return for the Monday Night Football matchup against the Dallas Cowboys on October 26.For now, all eyes remain on the Philadelphia Eagles’ Week 6 clash.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. New Orleans Saints wide receiver Devaughn Vele and tight end Juwan Johnson are Week 6 fantasy football starts against the New York Giants, while Alvin Kamara 's back injury pushes him to flex status and opens deep-flex value for Kendre Miller .

Chris Olave (illness) is questionable after missing practice Wednesday and Thursday before a limited session Friday, and Kamara (back) is questionable after three limited practices. Saints at Giants kicks off at 1 p.m. ET at MetLife Stadium.

New Orleans Saints wide receiver Devaughn Vele (14) celebrates a touchdown against the Detroit Lions | Lon Horwedel-Imagn Images

Vele leads all NFL receivers with 207 routes run , and his 91% snap share is the highest among New Orleans wideouts. That role has produced at least six targets in all five games, including nine in the Week 4 loss to Atlanta, when he caught six passes for 54 yards and a touchdown.

Minnesota held quarterback Tyler Shough to 96 passing yards in Week 5, and the 6-foot-5 receiver finished with four catches for 26 yards. The Giants are a softer test because they allow 25.4 half-PPR points per game to wide receivers , and they've ruled out cornerback Colton Hood (concussion) and safety Tyler Nubin (neck).

Olave ranks second in the NFL with 537 receiving yards, so his absence would make Vele the Saints' top wide receiver against a short-handed secondary. Even with Olave active, the former Utah walk-on's route volume makes him a WR3 with a steady floor, and he moves into WR2 range if Olave sits.

Juwan Johnson's matchup improves after Minnesota

New Orleans Saints tight end Juwan Johnson (83) looks on against Minnesota Vikings | Stephen Lew-Imagn Images

Johnson caught four of five targets for 16 yards against the Vikings , a defense that has allowed the second-fewest receptions to tight ends. That dud followed four straight games with at least 53 receiving yards, and he's totaled 248 yards, three touchdowns and five catches of 20-plus yards this season.

The Giants have allowed 33 catches to tight ends, tied for sixth-most in the league, and 10.9 half-PPR points per game to the position. Nubin's absence takes a starting safety out of coverage, and Johnson has seen seven red-zone targets, scoring from 1 and 2 yards out against Las Vegas in Week 3.

Johnson has drawn at least seven targets in three of five games, and that volume against a defense that gives up steady catches to tight ends makes him a TE1 start in Week 6.

New Orleans Saints running back Alvin Kamara (41) runs against Atlanta Falcons cornerback C.J. Henderson (26) | Stephen Lew-Imagn Images

Kamara played through the same back injury in Week 5 but logged a season-low 12 snaps, turning three carries into 12 yards and losing six yards on two catches. CJ Donaldson led the backfield in snaps while handling pass protection, and Miller took most of the carries.

The 31-year-old's Week 4 game against Atlanta showed what he offers when healthy: seven carries for 23 yards and two touchdowns, plus five catches for 35 yards. Travis Etienne Jr. (hamstring) remains on injured reserve, but coach Kellen Moore has made clear the Saints won't lean on one back.

"Very few times this league is one running back going to haul the load . That's just what this league is," Moore said.

New York has allowed 122.8 rushing yards per game, eighth-most in the NFL , and 19.6 half-PPR points per game to running backs. If he's active, Kamara is a flex play because of his receiving role, but another limited snap count would cap his output. Saints inactives are due at 11:30 a.m. ET.

New Orleans Saints running back Kendre Miller (5) runs against Detroit during | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

Miller handled 10 of the backfield's 17 carries against Minnesota, gaining 30 yards and scoring on a 2-yard run in the second quarter. He has 29 carries for 83 yards and two touchdowns this season.

The efficiency concerns are significant. Miller ranks 43rd among 44 qualifying backs with 1.45 yards after contact per attempt , and he ran one route last week without drawing a target, so his fantasy day depends on reaching the end zone.

Still, New York no longer has defensive tackle Dexter Lawrence in the middle and has given up 17 carries of 10-plus yards. Miller is a deep flex in 12-team and larger leagues as a goal-line bet, and he'd move into RB2 range as the lead runner if Kamara is inactive.

articles.title: Todd Gurley takes blame for Trump curse costing Georgia vs. Auburn
articles.summary: Georgia Bulldogs legend Todd Gurley jokingly blamed himself for his former team’s 27-24 loss to the Auburn Tigers on Saturday after accompanying President Do...
articles.body:
Georgia Bulldogs legend Todd Gurley jokingly blamed himself for his former team's 27-24 loss to the Auburn Tigers on Saturday after accompanying President Donald Trump to a political rally in Georgia the day before.

The No. 1-ranked Bulldogs suffered their first loss of the season Saturday at Sanford Stadium, surrendering an early 14-point advantage before Alex McPherson's 34-yard field goal capped Auburn's comeback as time expired.

Gurley, who traveled aboard Air Force One with Trump and attended his rally at Dalton Municipal Airport, reacted to Georgia's defeat on X (formerly Twitter).

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

"Damn I done made UGA lose," the former running back wrote, suggesting his appearance alongside the president might have brought bad luck to his alma mater.

Trump's Friday visit was organized to support Republican Senate nominee Mike Collins and gubernatorial nominee Rick Jackson ahead of Georgia's midterm elections. Gurley's participation continued the president's efforts to connect with prominent Georgia football figures while campaigning in the battleground state.

Gurley played for the Bulldogs from 2012 to 2014 before becoming a first-round NFL Draft selection by the Los Angeles Rams. He later earned NFL Offensive Player of the Year honors in 2017.

Georgia initially appeared in control, building a 14-0 lead in the first quarter. However, the Tigers responded with 24 unanswered points, putting the Bulldogs in a difficult position.

Quarterback Gunner Stockton helped Georgia recover from a 24-14 deficit, guiding a 94-yard touchdown drive that ended with a four-yard scoring pass to London Humphreys. Peyton Woodring's 42-yard field goal also contributed to the comeback, allowing the Bulldogs to level the score at 24.

Georgia's hopes of securing a late victory disappeared when Stockton fumbled with 58 seconds remaining while running from the Auburn 46-yard line. Tigers safety Sylvester Smith-Reed recovered the ball, and a roughing-the-passer penalty against Bulldogs outside linebacker Gabe Harris Jr. helped Auburn move into position for McPherson's game-winning kick.

Stockton finished with 272 passing yards, two touchdown passes and two interceptions on 22-of-34 passing. Tigers quarterback Byrum Brown excelled on the ground, recording 115 rushing yards and a touchdown on 26 carries while completing 15 of 26 passes for 150 yards and another score.

The loss ended Georgia's nine-game winning streak against Auburn and its run of 53 consecutive wins over unranked opponents. The Bulldogs fell to 6-1 overall and 4-1 in Southeastern Conference play, while the Tigers improved to 4-2 and 2-2 in the SEC.

Georgia will have a bye week before facing Florida on October 31 at Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta.

articles.title: Bill Belichick’s girlfriend Jordon Hudson has a tense history with Pulitzer Prize-winning journalist Pablo Torre, and the journalist is revisiting it
articles.summary: Pablo Torre says Jordon Hudson once told him on Instagram that she was suing. She never did.
articles.body: Pablo Torre says Jordon Hudson once told him on Instagram that she was suing. She never did. The Pulitzer Prize-winning journalist revisited that November 2025 post this week on "Front Office Sports Tonight." Hudson is the girlfriend of North Carolina coach Bill Belichick, and Torre has reported on her role around the program and her part in Belichick's business ventures. He said no case was ever filed, and he sounded a little let down about it. The Tar Heels visit Duke on Saturday, so the spotlight on Hudson shows no sign of dimming.Pablo Torre revisits Jordon Hudson's lawsuit threatThe post went up in November 2025. Jordan Hudson hinted she would take legal action against Torre, and that was the end of it. According to Torre, nothing was ever filed.He summed it up on the show. "She said on Instagram, 'P.S. I'm suing you,' and did not," Torre said.A clip from that appearance was shared on the show's X account.He added that the missing lawsuit left him with mixed feelings. It was a relief, sure. It was also a letdown, because he figured a trial would have been interesting. That joke tells you something about how he approaches the whole saga. Torre does not sound rattled. He sounds like a reporter who braced for a fight and never got one.Pablo Torre's reporting on Jordon Hudson goes beyond one postTorre has not treated Hudson as a footnote. On "Pablo Torre Finds Out," his Pulitzer Prize-winning podcast, he has spent segments on her relationship with Belichick. He has also examined her involvement in the University of North Carolina football program and in his business ventures.Belichick took over the Tar Heels in December 2024, and Hudson has been a steady presence since. The pair were recently spotted scouting high school players together, which only adds to the questions.That mix of personal and professional is what keeps the story alive. A coach's partner showing up on scouting trips and in business coverage is not something reporters can easily ignore.Other journalists have also reported on her since Belichick arrived.Jordon Hudson stays in the spotlight as North Carolina visits DukeHudson has not stayed quiet when stories about her land. She has pushed back on claims she believes are false, and the Instagram post fits that pattern, even without a lawsuit behind it.Belichick's name guarantees the attention. He spent decades as one of the NFL's biggest coaching names with the New England Patriots, and his move to college football carried that glare with him. Anyone beside him gets noticed, and questions about her role come with it.Almost two years into the job, Belichick is still fielding questions about more than football.For now, the football matters more. North Carolina is 3-2 and heads to Duke on Saturday. The Blue Devils are 4-1. A road win would give Belichick a better headline. articles.title: Human vs. ChatGPT NFL Week 6 betting picks: AI goes all-in on totals after another weekly win
articles.summary: ChatGPT beat its human rival for a second straight week in NFL betting, but the overall season unit lead is shrinking heading into Week 6 picks.
articles.body: OK, this is getting annoying. ChatGPT beat me in NFL betting for the second straight week, going 3-2 while I finished 2-3. The robot added 0.94 units to its total, while I gave back 1.26. It also won our only head-to-head matchup, backing San Francisco while I took Seattle. That's three straight losses for me in games where we picked opposite sides. NFL WEEK 5 SUNDAY TAKEAWAYS: RODGERS DEFIES FATHER TIME, COEN GETS BAILED OUT, 49ERS SURVIVE UGLY PERFORMANCE Apparently, telling the robot I was proud of it last week was a mistake. Now it has confidence. Before GPT gets too excited, though, I'm still the only one making money this season. I'm sitting at 13-11-1 and +1.26 units, while the machine is 11-14 and down 3.87 units. Yes, my lead is shrinking. No, I don't particularly want to talk about that. What I would like to talk about is the Eagles covering as my latest "plug your nose and hit place bet" pick. Apparently, the bets I hate making are the ones I should be making more often (4-0 this year). There's probably a lesson in there somewhere, but knowing me, I'll ignore it. Anyway, we've both got five more picks for Week 6. Let's see if I can give humanity something to celebrate again. Both of us get five selections from the same odds board, with a maximum price of -120. The stakes are adjusted so every winning bet produces one unit of profit. For example, -110 requires risking 1.10 units, while +110 requires 0.91 units. A push returns the stake and counts as zero units. Odds were captured Thursday at 8 p.m. ET. Before we get to the Week 6 picks, let’s review last week. Week 5 NFL Betting Results Dan’s Week 5 NFL Betting Picks (2-3, -1.26 units) The Eagles coasted to an easy cover in a game where they never trailed by more than 7 and would have won the game outright if not for Nick Sirianni's terrible late-game decision-making. Basically, my Sunday peaked before the early-afternoon games started and never really got better. I was way wrong about the Saints offense, as Tyler Shough threw for 96 yards in the loss. And I was even more wrong about the Patriots, who matched the entire 45-point total on their own. I stand by the Seahawks pick, and I’m still mad about Mike Macdonald calling an outside zone run from Seattle’s own 4-yard line with 18 seconds left in the first half. George Holani fumbled, and San Francisco recovered in the end zone. GPT’s Week 5 NFL Betting Picks (3-2, +0.94 units) GPT nailed Thursday Night Football as the nine-point underdog Bucs went into Dallas and upset the Cowboys. But it whiffed badly on the Raiders, who lost by 28. Yes, it got me on the 49ers-Seahawks bet, and I'm still mad about that fumble recovery in the end zone to close the first half. Not to keep tooting GPT's horn, but since its abysmal 2-8 start (including 0-5 in Week 1), the robot is now 9-6 over the past three weeks. SEASON REPORT CARD DAN: 13-11-1, +1.26 units GPT: 11-14, -3.87 units Dan’s Week 6 NFL Betting Card 1. Chicago Bears-Atlanta Falcons Under 52½ (-108) Chicago Bears at Atlanta Falcons, Sunday at 1 p.m. ET Dan’s analysis: I just think this total is too high. Caleb Williams is back, but I think he's going to be cautious coming off his hamstring injury and not use his legs as much. I also think the Bears staff wants to keep him healthy by establishing the run early and often. The Falcons have been putting up points since Michael Penix Jr. returned from injury, but I think their offense is due for a step back. I can see both teams running the ball a ton and keeping the clock moving, so I'll take the under. GPT’s analysis: The high total and both teams’ rushing production give your under a credible foundation. Chicago has also converted just 42.9% of its red-zone trips into touchdowns, making an efficient shootout less dependable. My concern is the defensive personnel: Chicago is missing Montez Sweat, Dayo Odeyingbo and T.J. Edwards, while Atlanta’s cornerback injuries give the Bears a favorable passing matchup. Those absences create scoring opportunities on both sides. I see the under argument, but the competing injury effects kept this outside my five. 2. Los Angeles Chargers +7½ (-110) Los Angeles Chargers at Kansas City Chiefs, Sunday at 4:25 p.m. ET Dan’s analysis: This is the official "Dan Z.’s Plug Your Nose and Hit 'Place Bet' Bet of the Week" (that's trademarked and don't you dare try to steal it from me). I just can't quit the Chargers. I refuse to believe that a team led by Justin Herbert is completely incapable of scoring points. Also, the Chiefs are 4-0 and a team the public generally likes to bet. So, I'll fade the likely public money and back the Chargers (again), even though it's going to feel terrible hitting that "place bet" button. GPT’s analysis: Getting more than a touchdown is the strongest argument for Los Angeles, especially with a defense performing better than its 0-5 record suggests. Kansas City is also missing Rashee Rice and Josh Simmons. My concern is the Chargers’ depleted offensive line and turnover problems against a rested Chiefs team. Stalled possessions and short fields could help Kansas City build separation without consistently beating that defense. I prefer under 41.5, but your +7.5 still cashes in a 24–17 Chiefs victory. The hook makes this considerably more appealing than +7. 3. Las Vegas Raiders +5½ (-110) Buffalo Bills at Las Vegas Raiders, Sunday at 4:25 p.m. ET Dan’s analysis: I’m not sure if I can have two "plug your nose" picks in one week, but this is another one that could easily qualify (I mean I make the rules so I can whatever I want, but I digress). Basically, I've decided I'm just fading the best teams in the NFL this week (this theme isn't done). The Raiders came out firing at 3-0 before suffering a heartbreaking loss against the Chiefs in Week 4 and then getting boatraced by the Patriots in Week 5. But this is more about the Bills. Buffalo is coming off a thrilling overtime win over the Los Angeles Rams on Monday Night Football. It's tough to recover on a short week after an overtime game. Plus, the Bills are playing back-to-back games out west in the Pacific Time Zone. I think Las Vegas can keep this close enough to cover. GPT’s analysis: Buffalo’s vulnerable pass defense gives Kirk Cousins and Brock Bowers a route to keeping Las Vegas competitive. The Bills are also coming off a Monday night overtime game, strengthening the home underdog’s case. My hesitation is Las Vegas’ defense, which allows 140.6 rushing yards per game and faces Josh Allen and James Cook. Buffalo could score efficiently without needing its questionable receivers at full strength. I prefer over 53.5, which can cash whether the Raiders keep this close or Buffalo creates separation. 4. Dallas Cowboys Moneyline (+101) Dallas Cowboys at Green Bay Packers, Sunday Night Football Dan’s analysis: In all honesty, this is all about fading public perception. Dallas is coming off an ugly Thursday Night Football loss to a previously winless Tampa Bay team starting rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels. On the other side, the Packers smashed a shorthanded Chicago Bears team. Basically, everyone thinks the Cowboys are bad and the Packers are good. The answer lies somewhere in the middle, so I'll take the plus money with Dallas because I think they're going to win this game. GPT’s analysis: Dallas’ productive offense and three extra rest days offer the best case for your pick. Green Bay has also lost defensive tackles Javon Hargrave and Jonathan Ford to injured reserve, creating an opportunity for the Cowboys’ running game. My concern is Dallas’ defense, which ranks last in EPA allowed per play. Jordan Love and Green Bay’s receivers have a favorable matchup at home. articles.title: Former NFL QB Sean Salisbury wants officials to face postgame questions just like players and coaches
articles.summary: Sean Salisbury says NFL officials should face on-camera postgame interviews to explain missed calls, just like players and coaches always do.
articles.body: NFL players and coaches have to answer questions after games, usually while they're still angry about whatever went wrong. Former NFL quarterback Sean Salisbury wants officials getting that same treatment when they're the ones who made the mistake. REDZONE HOST SCOTT HANSON DEFENDS NFL OFFICIATING, CALLS LEAGUE 'BEST OFFICIATED' IN AMERICA "I want to know what they saw on the field immediately after the game, when their emotions were up, just like the players and coaches," Salisbury told OutKick. We talked about missed calls, but also about the recent confrontations between officials and players. Watching some of those exchanges, I wondered why the people responsible for keeping things under control were getting so worked up themselves. "It's like officials are instigating certain situations," Salisbury said. Salisbury wants officials explaining what they saw after games Salisbury doesn't want to wait for somebody at the league office to explain a missed call the next day. He wants to hear from the person who made the decision, while the game is still fresh. The NFL has what's called a pool interview process where reporters covering a game can request an explanation of a particular call. A designated pool reporter asks the questions, and a transcript of the answers is distributed to the rest of the media. That's where some of the referee explanations you read in game stories come from. But I'd like to see officials take questions on camera after games as routinely as players and coaches do. If a quarterback has to talk about why he threw a crucial fourth-quarter interception, or a coach has to face a grilling about a questionable fourth-down decision, then a referee can explain why he missed an obvious call. Salisbury repeatedly expressed respect for the job officials do. But he's frustrated by mistakes he believes should be obvious without somebody needing to slow down a replay and draw circles on the screen. "You can't miss the ones that the naked eye can see," he said. "You just can't. That's their gig." He also wondered whether replay has made some officials more hesitant to make a call themselves. Salisbury described it as a "security blanket," suggesting that knowing there's another opportunity to get something right can affect the initial decision. Salisbury pointed to the NFL’s recent suspensions of two officials as an example of the league holding them accountable. On Oct. 5, it suspended line judge Jeff Seeman for two games and referee Adrian Hill for one following separate Week 4 confrontations with players. SUPER BOWL CHAMPION BRUCE ARIANS RIPS 'OUT OF CONTROL' NFL REFS AFTER TWO SUSPENSIONS Seeman was caught on video appearing to yell "F–k you" at Cardinals tight end Trey McBride during Arizona's game against the Giants. Hill yelled at Vikings linebacker Eric Wilson after Wilson was accidentally knocked into him during Minnesota's game against Miami. Wilson later said Hill accepted his apology and explanation. Keeping your emotions out of it is part of the job During our conversation, Salisbury said officials are held to a higher standard. I told him I'd describe it a little differently. Players should be held to a high standard, too. They're on television in front of millions of people and they make a lot of money to play football. But an official has a different responsibility when an argument starts, because he's supposed to be the person who can settle it. I umpire high school baseball during the spring, and I've had plenty of parents chirp at me about calls. Do people say things that get under your skin? Of course. I don't get to start cursing at them because I've decided I've heard enough. Dealing with that frustration is part of the job I agreed to do. That's why I don't find "officials are human" to be much of an explanation for these confrontations. Sure, they're human. So am I. Being annoyed doesn't relieve you of the responsibility to keep your own emotions out of the game. Salisbury agreed with that distinction. "Your job is not there to pour gasoline," he said. He said the best officials know how to settle a confrontation before it gets worse. Sometimes that means calming a player down, and sometimes it means being firm. Either way, the official has to keep the game moving without turning a disagreement into something personal. And getting into it with a player can follow an official long after that particular argument ends. Salisbury pointed out that the next disputed call might then look personal to the team that was just arguing with him. "You start to think, well, if you miss a call later on against the team, well, he had it in for us," he said. OUTKICK IS NOW AVAILABLE ON THE FOX NEWS APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD Salisbury also brought up gambling and the conspiracy theories that come with disputed calls. Fans who think an official just cost them a winning bet are already going to question what happened. Watching that official get into a shouting match with a player gives them something else to point to. I'd much rather hear the official explain what he saw than spend the next day watching people guess at his motives. Put him on camera after the game, while the coach is still answering questions about the loss. And if the official got it wrong, he can say that, too. "We hold players accountable. I think officials need to be held accountable," Salisbury said.

articles.title: Tyler Shough Injured, Latest Rumors on Saints QB's Status and Timeline for Recovery
articles.summary: New Orleans Saints quarterback Tyler Shough hasn't missed any time, but he is reportedly playing through multiple broken bones in his left hand.
articles.body:
New Orleans Saints quarterback Tyler Shough hasn't missed any time, but he is reportedly playing through multiple broken bones in his left hand.

ESPN's Adam Schefter reported Sunday there are two broken bones in Shough's non-throwing hand that one source said would take "a couple of months" to fully heal even while he continues to play. He first suffered the setback during New Orleans' 45-24 loss to the Atlanta Falcons on Oct 5.

While Shough has fully participated in practice and, according to Schefter, remains "determined to play through any injury," he has been handing off with his opposite hand and playing with his ring and pinky fingers taped together.

What's more, he has worn a protective glove on the bandaged hand and is expected to do so again for Sunday's contest against the New York Giants.

Shough has solid numbers overall and has completed 66.8 percent of his passes for 1,299 yards, nine touchdowns and five interceptions. However, his production has not been the same since suffering the injury against the Falcons.

He threw for 255 yards, four touchdowns and one interception the previous week against the Las Vegas Raiders but had just one touchdown against the Falcons. Then he turned in the worst game of his season while throwing for just 96 yards, zero touchdowns and two interceptions in a loss to the Minnesota Vikings.

New Orleans is now 1-4 on the season and needs to turn things around quickly if it is going to be a realistic factor in the NFC playoff race.

The plan seems to be to continue with Shough, but his performance will undoubtedly be under a microscope with the injury and following his poor showing against the Vikings. Spencer Rattler is his backup, although he is just 1-13 as a starter since entering the league in the 2024 NFL draft.

The Saints' Week 8 bye is just two weeks away, so there will at least be some time in the near future for Shough to further recover.

articles.title: Cam Skattebo Loses Snaps, Latest Giants Rumors and Fantasy Outlook for Najee Harris, RB Committee
articles.summary: Fantasy managers relying on New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo, beware.
articles.body:
Fantasy managers relying on New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo, beware.

He reportedly is in line for fewer opportunities during Sunday's game against the New Orleans Saints.

ESPN's Jordan Raanan reported the "expectation" is New York will "change" its running back rotation to more of a committee approach with "Skattebo downgraded but still part of the mix after the fumbles" and Najee Harris assuming "a larger role."

It won't just be those two, though, as Tyrone Tracy and Devin Singletary are also expected to be active.

Singletary and Tracy have not been a significant part of the running back rotation to this point. The former has just nine carries, while the latter has just seven.

By comparison, Skattebo has 81 carries and Harris has 27.

None of the running backs have been particularly effective with Skattebo's and Harris' 3.6 yards per carry tied for the highest mark. Skattebo has at least been a factor in the passing game with 10 catches, which is third on the Giants behind only Isaiah Likely and Malik Nabers.

However, he has already fumbled three times, including a critical one in overtime in the Giants' tie against the Washington Commanders in their last game. They were already in field-goal range and would have won with a made kick, although they were also fortunate enough to walk away with a tie considering Washington's clock management blunder on the ensuing possession ended the game.

From a fantasy perspective, it is difficult to trust any of these running backs.

The production alone has been disappointing, and playing even more of a rotation will only cut into Skattebo's opportunities in particular. Harris may be worth a stash on the bench to see how he responds to an uptick in chances, as he could eventually work his way further up the depth chart with an impressive performance against the Saints.

But for the immediate future, it is probably best for fantasy managers to turn elsewhere in their starting lineups.

NFL referee Larry Smith was carted off the field during Sunday's game between the Houston Texans and Jacksonville Jaguars.

Smith fell backwards as he tried catching the game ball from the sideline between plays. He was unable to put much weight on his left leg:

Pro Football Talk's Mike Florio noted last year, when referee Adrian Hill exited mid-game, the NFL doesn't have much of a contingency plan in the event an official goes down. The rest of the crew is expected to pick up the slack rather than have a standby replacement at the ready.

According to Football Zebras , the league assigned Smith to Shawn Hochuli's crew as the umpire prior to the start of the 2026 season. This is just his second year as an NFL referee. He previously worked games in the Big Ten and UFL.

Given what appeared to be the severity of the injury, the NFL will need to find a substitute for Smith in Week 7, and his availability for the rest of the season could be in doubt.

articles.title: NFL umpire Larry Smith carted off early after slipping on wet field in London
articles.summary: Larry Smith appeared to sustain a lower-leg injury early Sunday.
articles.body:
The Sunday slate in Week 6 began in one of the worst ways possible: with an injury. It wasn't a player on either the Jacksonville Jaguars or Houston Texans who went down, however; it was umpire Larry Smith.

Smith needed to be carted off the field after he appeared to sustain a lower-leg injury after falling on the field.

Smith was injured in between plays. The broadcast showed a replay of Smith's fall. While he was initially able to get up, he started limping after taking a step or two and was forced to go back down to the ground.

With Smith presumably out for the rest of the game, the contest will feature six members of an officiating crew instead of the usual seven.

Smith is a long-time Big 10 official who finally got the call to the NFL last season. This was his second year on the job. When he's not officiating, Smith is a principal at a Kansas City school.

He spoke about his promotion to the NFL on a local news program last year.

As the umpire for Sunday's game, Smith was tasked with standing behind the offensive players and watching for offensive line penalties or other offensive infractions.

That task will now be filled by another member of the officiating crew Sunday.

articles.title: NFL monitors France street violence before Saints-Steelers game near Paris with a major decision looming
articles.summary: The NFL is monitoring street violence across France ahead of the New Orleans Saints vs. Pittsburgh Steelers game at Stade de France in Paris.
articles.body: The NFL is monitoring the street violence in France with no current plan to move its first-ever game in the country scheduled for next Sunday just north of Paris, but a league source said that can change if events warrant playing in a different venue. Street violence erupted across France on Saturday when peaceful marches of 500,000 to 800,000 people, according to reports, devolved into masked groups clashing with police, looting businesses and setting fire to private property and public buildings, including the historic city hall in Limoges. Reports on Sunday cited arrests climbing from 1,000 to 1,800, including 855 in the Paris region. LIMOGES TOWN HALL 'LARGELY LOST' AFTER FAR-LEFT RIOTERS SET HISTORIC BUILDING ON FIRE AMID FRENCH UNREST The violence in France has gotten the attention of governments worldwide, including the United States. President Donald Trump posted on Sunday morning on Truth Social that "France is burning" and that "people with hatred in their hearts" have "shattered that once great country." FRANCE EXPLODES AGAIN AS STUDENTS RIOT OVER EDUCATION That potentially affects the NFL because it is scheduled to play at the Stade de France in Saint-Denis just north of Paris next Sunday when the New Orleans Saints "host" the Pittsburgh Steelers in a regular season game. The league's position on the game last week was that the game in Paris is a go. "We look forward to welcoming fans to Paris later this month," the league said in a statement. ROGER GOODELL DETAILS NFL EXPANSION POSSIBILITIES AND A TIMETABLE FOR A FULL SEASON OF INTERNATIONAL GAMES But that was before things became violent. The NFL's chief spokesperson did not respond to an email from OutKick and Fox News Digital for clarification on the matter after the violence erupted. But a league source, who requested anonymity, told OutKick on Sunday that the league has been working "with local authorities and partners on all operational and security matters and if events warrant, a change in venue can be considered." The Saints and Steelers have previously shown the requisite amount of excitement about playing the league's inaugural France game. "Louisiana's relationship with France is centuries deep, and this game represents another meaningful step in strengthening those cultural and economic ties," Saints owner Gayle Benson said in a statement announcing the game. articles.title: Kansas City Chiefs' $4.5 billion Kansas investment gains momentum with new real-estate venture
articles.summary: The Kansas City Chiefs are planning a future that extends well beyond football.
articles.body: The Kansas City Chiefs are planning a future that extends well beyond football. In 2026, the franchise joined forces with Hunt Midwest to launch Two-Point Development, a real-estate venture designed to shape two major districts in Kansas. One will surround the team's planned domed stadium in Kansas City, Kansas, while the other will grow around its future headquarters and training facility in Olathe. The plan aims to connect sports, entertainment, housing and local businesses, turning the Chiefs' relocation into a broader development project with long-term implications for the Kansas City region.Kansas City Chiefs launch Two-Point Development with Hunt MidwestThe Chiefs and Hunt Midwest announced Two-Point Development on August 31, 2026. The new venture will lead the planning and development of mixed-use districts around both facilities, bringing together the team's sports and entertainment expertise with Hunt Midwest's real-estate experience.The partnership is a significant step in the Chiefs' planned move from Missouri to Kansas. Rather than treating the new stadium and training centre as separate construction projects, the organisations want to create connected destinations that attract people throughout the year.Chiefs chairman and CEO Clark Hunt described the partnership as an important moment for the family business.“This is a monumental day for our family as the Kansas City Chiefs and Hunt Midwest form a new business partnership,” Chiefs Chairman and CEO Clark Hunt said.“My father was a visionary who believed in the future of Kansas City and spent decades investing in the business community of this region. Today we are so proud that his football franchise and his real estate company are joining forces to drive transformational real estate developments around the Chiefs future stadium and training facility.""This partnership will create two dynamic districts, provide memorable experiences for residents and visitors, spur meaningful economic growth, and fundamentally transform the footprint of the Kansas City metro area. We are proud of this joint venture and excited to get to work making this vision a reality.”The name Two-Point Development also reflects the franchise's history. It draws inspiration from the two-point conversion, a rule associated with the American Football League that founder Lamar Hunt helped bring into professional football.The new company will act as master developer, overseeing architects, engineers, land planners and contractors responsible for bringing the plans to life. However, the announcement outlines a development vision rather than a completed list of buildings, tenants or opening dates for the surrounding districts.Chiefs stadium district in Kansas, Kansas, aims to become a year-round destinationThe first major development will surround the Chiefs' planned domed stadium in Wyandotte County, Kansas City, Kansas. The stadium is expected to open for the 2031 NFL season and become the centrepiece of a much larger entertainment destination.The proposed district is intended to offer more than a place to watch football. Plans call for a mix of entertainment, hospitality, retail, residential and public gathering spaces. If delivered as envisioned, the development could give fans more reasons to arrive early, stay after games and visit even when the Chiefs are not playing.That broader approach could also create opportunities for local businesses. Restaurants, hotels, shops and entertainment operators may benefit from visitors attending NFL games, concerts and other events. Nearby communities could gain new places to meet, work and spend time.Still, the success of the project will depend on execution. The quality of transport links, access to the stadium, parking arrangements and the range of attractions will help determine whether the district remains active beyond major events.The Chiefs have also released initial plans for a stadium designed to hold approximately 70,000 fans. The enclosed venue is intended to support a range of events, giving the wider development a potential draw throughout the year.Olathe headquarters and training facility will anchor a second development districtThe second part of the Two-Point Development plan centres on the Chiefs' future headquarters and training facility in Olathe, Johnson County. While the stadium district will be built around major events and large crowds, the Olathe project will also serve the team's everyday operations.The planned facility is expected to become the club's main workplace for football staff and players. The surrounding mixed-use district is intended to combine football, community activities, entertainment and other amenities in one connected area.The vision includes spaces where residents can live, work and spend their free time, alongside public areas that welcome visitors. That could make the development relevant to people who do not attend NFL games or follow the Chiefs closely.The location also creates a different set of opportunities from the stadium site. A headquarters and training centre operates throughout the week, bringing staff and other visitors to the area beyond game days. Nearby businesses could serve those regular users as well as people visiting the district for recreation or events.The two developments will have different roles, but the Chiefs and Hunt Midwest intend to apply a shared approach to planning, design and visitor experience. The challenge will be ensuring each district reflects its local surroundings rather than simply repeating the same mix of shops and attractions.For Olathe, the project could reshape the area around the new facility. Its lasting value, however, will depend on which businesses arrive, how the district connects with existing neighbourhoods and whether residents find the new amenities useful.Chiefs' $4.5 billion Kansas project carries major economic ambitionsTwo-Point Development is part of a wider Kansas investment plan that the Chiefs estimated at $4.5 billion in June 2026. The overall figure includes a projected $3 billion stadium in Wyandotte County, a $300 million headquarters and practice facility in Olathe, and $1.2 billion in private real-estate development around the two sites.Those figures represent projected capital investment, not money already spent or guaranteed economic gains. The distinction matters because construction costs and economic benefits measure different things.An economic assessment commissioned by the Chiefs projected that the investment could generate $8.2 billion in one-time regional economic impact during construction. Once the stadium and other facilities become operational, team activity and visitor spending are projected to generate $1.5 billion in annual economic impact. These are forecasts, not guaranteed results.The construction phase could also support jobs across building, engineering, hospitality and related industries. Over time, the districts may create further employment in retail, food service, entertainment and property management. Local governments will be watching closely to see how much of that activity translates into lasting benefits for residents.Public financing is another important part of the wider project. Kansas has outlined a STAR bonds district intended to capture new sales tax revenue to help finance the stadium, the training facility and portions of the surrounding developments. The precise distribution of costs, revenues and long-term benefits will remain an important issue as the project advances.For the Chiefs, the move represents more than a change of home stadium. Two-Point Development gives the franchise a direct role in shaping the places around its facilities, with Hunt Midwest bringing established development experience to the partnership.The ambition is clear: build two districts that remain useful and attractive beyond football season. articles.title: Saints vs. Steelers Paris Game Addressed by NFL amid Protests in France
articles.summary: The NFL will continue ahead with a Week 7 meeting between the New Orleans Saints and Pittsburgh Steelers in Paris on Oct. 25.
articles.body:
The NFL will continue ahead with a Week 7 meeting between the New Orleans Saints and Pittsburgh Steelers in Paris on Oct. 25.

France has seen massive protests in the capital city and elsewhere. Buildings and streets have been significantly damaged as a result of the demonstrations.

For now, the NFL is proceeding with no expected changes to its plans.

"We continue to work closely with local authorities and partners on all operational and security matters," the league wrote in a statement to Front Office Sports' Mark Maske . "We are also providing the two clubs with regular updates. There's been no disruption or impact at league sites."

This is the first year the NFL has taken a game to France as part of its International Series. The Stade de France, which is traditionally used for the French national soccer and rugby teams, is the staging ground.

The game will kick off at 9:30 a.m. ET (2:30 p.m. CEST).

There are three more games after Week 7 in the International Series. The league will head to Madrid (Week 9), Munich (Week 10) and Mexico City (Week 11).

Moving a game outside of the United States at a late juncture isn't unprecedented for the NFL. Citing poor field conditions, a 2018 meeting between the Kansas City Chiefs and Los Angeles Rams was shifted to Los Angeles from Mexico City.

The Saints have Week 8 bye following their trip to Paris, so they'll get added time to reset from the long flight or if there are any logistical challenges presented by changing the location.

That's not a luxury afforded to the Steelers as they play the rival Cleveland Browns on Nov. 1.

The NFL's 2026 international series has gotten off to a solid start, with games in Australia and Brazil followed by two matchups in London. Now, the fifth international game of the season, and third in London, features the Jacksonville Jaguars and Houston Texans at Wembley Stadium in Week 6. However, ahead of kickoff, pregame rain swept through, muddying the field and complicating conditions for players and even the refs.

After a ref went down injured and had to be carted off, the field conditions were called into question, and the NFL world was quick to rip the NFL and Wembley for the conditions.

Fans Critical of Field Conditions During the Jaguars-Texans London Game

While debates over NFL playing surfaces often focus on synthetic turf, natural and hybrid grass fields can also draw criticism when conditions deteriorate. However, Wembley's hybrid grass pitch struggled after pregame rain left the surface slick, making it a hot topic of discussion.

Radio host Rick Ballou described what the entire NFL world was watching at Wembley to start the Jaguars-Texans AFC South showdown in London, saying, "Playing surface sucks in London, guys are on skates."

Former NFL defensive back and two-time Super Bowl champion Asante Samuel was quick to criticize the NFL for the state of the field.

He posted, "How does a widely successful company like the NFL continue to put athletes on these terrible fields risking players health???"

Another user couldn't help but agree with Samuel's criticism, saying, "The Field is Atrocious this week in London 🧐 NFL has to stop letting this happen."

Connie Carberg, the first female scout in the NFL, couldn't believe the timing of the broadcast's comments on the field's conditions, explaining, "Talking about how slippery the field in London is pre-game, and now refs slip and get carted off!! #InternationalGames #NFL"

articles.title: New NFL Rumors on Bo Nix's Struggles, Changes to Broncos' Offense Under Sean Payton
articles.summary: Denver Broncos quarterback Bo Nix has reportedly been struggling to adjust to the team's constant changes on the offensive side of the ball.
articles.body:
Denver Broncos quarterback Bo Nix has reportedly been struggling to adjust to the team's constant changes on the offensive side of the ball.

During this week's episode of Fox NFL Sunday , Jay Glazer provided some insight into the situation Nix has been dealing with after head coach Sean Payton took over play-calling duties from offensive coordinator Davis Webb.

"You know, I asked a bunch of people about that, and I didn't know this until this past week, is that when Davis Webb took over, he completely changed the terminology, the offensive side of the ball, for Bo Nix. Now that Sean Payton's taking it back over, it's like going back to a whole different language that you used to know," Glazer explained. "So I think at this point, man, [Nix's] head is just spinning, and you guys know. An offensive terminology, it's like learning a whole different language out there."

Payton had announced before Week 5 that he was taking back play-calling duties from Webb. Despite earning back-to-back wins, including a 17-14 overtime victory over the defending champion Seattle Seahawks on Thursday Night Football , Nix has shown no signs of improvement.

Denver's defense played 82 snaps in Thursday's win over Seattle, as Nix led an offense that produced just 168 yards and didn't have a drive longer than five plays on its last nine possessions of regulation. The team's longest play of the game was 16 yards.

After the game, Nix admitted that the offense has been disjointed, largely due to its lack of explosive plays.

"We're definitely capable [of better]. I don't know where the disconnect is right now to be honest with you," Nix said. "I just think we're really struggling to find those explosive plays, and that's what makes an offensive spectacular is explosive plays and right now we don't have those."

Still, at 4-2, the Broncos remain one of the best teams in the AFC. They will try to get their offense back on track when they face the Arizona Cardinals next Sunday.

articles.title: Travis Hunter Makes Rare NFL History with Unique Stat in Breakout Game for Jaguars vs. Texans
articles.summary: The Travis Hunter two-way experiment had its biggest success to date in Sunday's game between the Jacksonville Jaguars and Houston Texans.
articles.body:
The Travis Hunter two-way experiment had its biggest success to date in Sunday's game between the Jacksonville Jaguars and Houston Texans.

Hunter scored on a seven-yard touchdown pass in the fourth quarter to bring Jacksonville to within three points, 31-28.

On Houston's next possession, the second-year star intercepted a pass from Texans quarterback C.J. Stroud.

Before Hunter, nobody had notched a touchdown reception and interception in the same NFL game for 24 years:

The 2024 Heisman Trophy winner was limited to seven appearances as a rookie, and his usage as a two-way player was sporadic. To open the 2026 season, the Jags have lined him up almost exclusively on defense. He had logged 249 snaps on defense to just 21 on the other side of the ball, per Pro Football Reference .

In September, Jacksonville coach Liam Coen indicated he had plans to get Hunter more looks at receiver, but that yet to materialize prior to Week 6.

Maybe the coaching staff is finally making good on that. Hunter's 59 receiving yards against Houston were his third-most in a game, and he doubled his career touchdown reception output.

It's doubtful the 6'1" wide receiver/cornerback will match the kind of workload he had in college at Colorado. Playing 100-plus snaps every week in a 17-game season is unsustainable.

Hunter's game might at least be evolving to where he can be a shutdown corner and situational pass-catcher to great effect.

articles.title: Travis Hunter Shines & Marvin Harrison Jr. Debuts, Box Score Stats & Highlights for Texans vs. Jags
articles.summary: The Houston Texans are fighting back.
articles.body:
After starting the season 0-4, the Texans have now won two in a row after Ka'imi Fairbairn's 49-yard field goal gave them a 34-31 victory over the Jacksonville Jaguars on Sunday in London.

C.J. Stroud was brilliant in the team's first game after it traded for Marvin Harrison Jr. and outdueled Trevor Lawrence in the AFC South showdown. Other than Travis Hunter's late interception, Stroud didn't make any mistakes and directed the field-goal drive to improve to 2-4.

As for the Jaguars, they are 4-2 after their three-game winning streak came to an end.

While Harrison made his first catch as a Texan in the opening half, he wasn't much of a factor in the early going.

Houston's top option in Nico Collins was, though, as he hauled in a 42-yard reception to set up Foster Moreau's touchdown in the first quarter. That was just the start of the day for Moreau, who caught another touchdown in the final seconds of the first half to give the Texans a 17-14 advantage at intermission.

His second touchdown came after Stroud unleashed an incredible throw to Jaylin Noel under pressure as the two quarterbacks traded impressive plays. Lawrence bounced back from an early interception to Calen Bullock in the end zone—which came after a controversial holding penalty overturned a touchdown—with two touchdown passes to Bhayshul Tuten.

Lawrence set up the second touchdown with a strike to Hunter after showing his typical chemistry with Parker Washington against a Texans defense that lost Reed Blankenship to injury.

But momentum fully belonged to Houston after the second touchdown to Moreau, and it continued after halftime when a special-teams penalty by Jacksonville on a punt prolonged a drive that Stroud ended with another beautiful throw for a touchdown to Noel after Harrison was move involved.

All that meant was it was Lawrence's turn to respond, as the quarterback showdown continued when the Jaguars answered with a touchdown pass to Nate Boerkircher.

It was the rookie tight end who did the most work with an astounding one-handed catch for his first career touchdown, although Houston bounced right back with a first-career touchdown of its own when Jawhar Jordan broke free for a 25-yard score.

The touchdowns kept coming when the Jaguars turned to Hunter on offense for three catches on the ensuing drive, the last of which found the end zone.

Just when it seemed like Houston was going to put the game away with a long touchdown drive in the final minutes, the two-way star picked off Stroud in the end zone to give Lawrence and the Jaguars offense a chance to win it.

They didn't win it, although they tied it with a 60-yard field goal from Cam Little. Although he made it, Jaguars head coach Liam Coen probably has second thoughts about not going for the 4th-and-4 because he put the game back in the hands of Stroud and Co.

Stroud hit Woody Marks to move into field-goal range, and Fairbairn won it for the Texans.

They now have plenty of momentum heading into a matchup with the New York Giants, while Jacksonville has some questions to answer going into its bye.

articles.title: NFL London games 2026: Houston Texans beat Jacksonville Jaguars after Ka'imi Fairbairn's walk-off field goal
articles.summary: CJ Stroud throws three touchdown passes as the Houston Texans beat the Jacksonville Jaguars thanks to a game-winning field goal from Ka'imi Fairbairn in the final seconds at Wembley Stadium; Travis Hunter records touchdown and interception for Jaguars
articles.body:
It was a game that began with referee Larry Smith being carted off with a non-contact injury in the opening seconds. A game that spent its interval staging on-field Corgi races. And a game that concluded with another dose of boot-fuelled drama following Cam Little's last-second winner against the Philadelphia Eagles at Tottenham the previous week.

Texans quarterback CJ Stroud threw for 312 yards and three touchdowns while Jaylin Noel led his side with four receptions for 107 yards and a score as Houston improved to 2-4 on the year.

Stroud's first interception of the season came by way of Travis Hunter as the two-way Jags star became the first player to score a touchdown and record a pick in the same game since Brian Dawkins for the Philadelphia Eagles against the Texans on September 29, 2002.

Trevor Lawrence finished 24 of 41 for 306 yards, four touchdowns and one interception as the Jaguars slipped to 4-2 at the end of their fortnight in the UK.

Hunter had derailed Houston's attempt to put the game to bed with four minutes left when he intercepted Stroud in the end zone to halt a 12-play drive.

Last week's hero Little delivered again moments later when he converted a 60-yard field goal to tie the game at 31-31 with two minutes to play.

Stroud proceeded to navigate a game-winning drive that included a 19-yard connection to Woody Marks on third-and-two as Houston reached field goal range to set up Fairbairn's defining moment. He delivered on cue.

Having led 17-14 at the break, Houston pushed their lead out to 24-14 on the opening drive of the second half through Noel's 13-yard touchdown catch on third-and-10.

Jacksonville's reply came courtesy of a one-handed one-yard touchdown grab by tight end Nate Boerkircher to pull within 24-21 after Jakobi Meyers had springboarded the drive with two catches for a combined 50 yards.

Jawhar Jordan, elevated from the practice squad for Sunday's game, scurried clear for a 25-yard touchdown on the ensuing possession as Houston opened up a 10-point cushion.

Back came the Jags, Hunter taming a bullet from Lawrence for a seven-yard touchdown to make it 31-28 after the extra point with 11.26 to play in the fourth quarter.

Houston had struck first in the game when Stroud floated a six-yard touchdown pass to tight end Foster Moreau, rewarding Nico Collins for his 42-yard airborne contested catch in direct coverage from Hunter along the sideline.

The Jags were foiled in their immediate response when Bhayshul Tuten's three-yard touchdown run was nullified by a Brenton Strange holding penalty, before Lawrence was intercepted by Calen Bullock in the end zone while targeting Jakobi Meyers on third-and-goal.

Tuten refused to be denied again when he slalomed through two tackle attempts for a 27-yard touchdown catch-and-run mid-way through the second quarter.

The Jags running back struck again when Lawrence peeled out to his right to float a two-yard strike to Tuten for a 14-10 lead with a minute remaining in the half. Houston responded instantly when Moreau hauled in a one-yard touchdown pass with eight seconds left after Noel's 50-yard reception.

articles.title: Ryan Fitzpatrick responds to Aqib Talib, sort of
articles.summary: After Prime Video's Ryan Fitzpatrick teed off on Broncos quarterback Bo Nix following Thursday night's overtime win over the Seahawks, former NFL cornerback...
articles.body:
After Prime Video's Ryan Fitzpatrick teed off on Broncos quarterback Bo Nix following Thursday night's overtime win over the Seahawks, former NFL cornerback Aqib Talib chastised Fitzpatrick with a long recital of his career accomplishments.

Fitzpatrick had the next word, which is likely not the last word. Fitzpatrick posted a video in which he pretends to be talking to Talib , using clips from Talib's rant.

It's comical. And Fitzpatrick seems to be doing his best to have fun with it.

The only hint of a slap at Talib comes near the very end, when Fitzpatrick says, "This really has me questioning all my life decisions."

Talib has a documented history of not-so-great life decisions away from football. And but for the fight at a youth football game that resulted in Talib's brother shooting and killing a man , Talib would have been Fitzpatrick's Thursday Night Football on-air colleague.

So the ball is now back in Talib's court. It's hard to imagine him not responding to Fitzpatrick.

articles.title: Report: 'No change is imminent' from Saints owner Gayle Benson
articles.summary: Sounds like Gayle Benson is all talk. ESPN reports 'the indication is that no change is imminent' after the Saints owner criticized her coach and GM.
articles.body:
So much for Gayle Benson's strong words about the team she owns underperforming. Days after naming head coach Kellen Moore and general manager Mickey Loomis among those responsible for a 1-4 record through five games she called "not acceptable," Benson was seen politely hugging and chatting with Moore at New Orleans Saints practice on Friday. And this new report makes it sound like she's all talk and no action.

ESPN's Ian Rapoport wrote that "according to those who know: Benson supports Moore and the coaching staff, and the indication is that no change is imminent."

That's probably the worst thing you could read after this. The Saints have gotten worse by the week -- increasingly undisciplined, harder to watch, and slowing down offensively as the season marches on. The defense has fallen apart and the special teams units have been at fault on too many negative plays. Moore hasn't shown he has the answers to solve the problems he and Loomis have created, or to respond to the challenges out of their control. And they're just going to ride this out?

If your goal is to see the Saints punt on this season and lock up a top-three pick in the 2027 NFL Draft, you might be in luck. It's possible Rapoport's sources are wrong and a 1-6 or 2-5 record at the bye week would be enough to push Benson into action. But right now, based on what we can see and what's going around, it's tough to see the Saints giving fans much reason for optimism any time soon.
